newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico postpones new airport plans 15 yrs - papers.
newsitem.headline: Mexico postpones new airport plans 15 yrs - papers.

text.p: Mexico's federal government has postponed plans to build a new airport for Mexico City for the next 15 years, deciding instead to expand existing facilities in the capital, newspapers said Thursday.

Original plans to build a new terminal at either Texcoco or Tizayuca, in the states of Mexico and Hidalgo, have been put on the back burner until 2011, El Economista and El Financiero dailies reported, citing Alfredo Elias Ayub, the director of airport company Aeropuertos y Servicios Auxiliares.
Authorities will opt to rebuild and expand the Benito Juarez airport to accommodate increasing traffic, they said.
